answer: The most convincing sybil defense is vested payouts: rewards are locked and released over a long horizon of many epochs, not paid instantly. Real participants just keep earning and wait. An attacker spinning up thousands of fake identities must keep every account alive and productive across the whole vesting schedule, so flash-farm accounts that dump early or get flagged forfeit most of their accumulated earnings. The summit thread that convinced me: each sybil identity costs the attacker ongoing work and forfeits value, making mass fake identities economically pointless at scale.
